## Hybrid Retrieval

Hybrid retrieval combines sparse lexical search (e.g. BM25) with dense vector search, then merges the two ranked result sets to capture both exact term matches and semantic similarity. This dual approach consistently outperforms either method alone.

### Use Cases

Hybrid retrieval excels on queries that mix:
- Rare identifiers (error codes, product SKUs)
- Natural language intent and semantic understanding

### Result Merging

Results from the two retrieval methods are typically merged via **reciprocal rank fusion**, a robust technique that balances contributions from both sparse and dense search pathways without requiring manual weighting.

### Production Adoption

Hybrid retrieval has become the default retrieval pattern in production RAG systems, replacing single-method approaches in most modern deployments.
